cards.text: On the twenty-fourth day of the same month, the Israelites gather together. They're fasting and wearing sackcloth, with dust on their heads. I had dust on MY head for years in that junk drawer, friend, but these folks put it there on purpose.

cards.question: The people of Israelite descent separate themselves from all the foreigners. Then they stand up. What do they do?

answers.text: Confess their sins and their fathers' sins
Bring offerings to the house of God
Choose new leaders for the whole city

cards.text: They stand in their places and read from the Book of the Law for a quarter of the day, then spend another quarter in confession and worship. A quarter of a day standing? I LIVE on a gold base, friend, and I'd still be looking around for a chair.
Then the Levites stand on the raised platform and cry out to the LORD their God in a loud voice. LOUD loud. Mags, my little bell, would've been so proud.

cards.question: Up on the platform, the Levites call out to the crowd to stand up. What for?

answers.text: To bless the LORD their God
To march out to the city gates

cards.text: Then the Levites pray, calling God's name glorious and exalted above all blessing and praise. And buckle up, friend, because this prayer is taking the LONG way around.

cards.question: The Levites' prayer walks through a whole lot of history. Where does it start?

answers.text: With God creating the heavens and the earth
With Moses leading Israel out of Egypt
With David bringing the ark to Jerusalem

cards.text: Next the prayer gets to Abram. God chose him and brought him out of Ur of the Chaldeans.

cards.question: God also gives Abram a new name: ___.
God made a covenant to give the land to Abraham's descendants, and the Levites say He has kept that promise.

cards.text: Then the prayer moves to Egypt, where God saw the affliction of Israel's fathers and heard their cry at the Red Sea. He performed signs and wonders against Pharaoh, king of Egypt, his officials and all the people of his land.

cards.question: The Levites give a reason God sent signs and wonders against Pharaoh and his people. What is it?

answers.text: They acted with arrogance against Israel's fathers
They broke a treaty they made with Israel
They wanted Israel's land for themselves

cards.text: God divides the sea, His people cross on dry ground, and the ones chasing them get hurled into the depths like a stone into raging waters. Then He leads His people with a pillar of cloud by day.

cards.question: By day, a pillar of cloud guides Israel. By night, a pillar of ___ lights the way.

cards.text: Then God comes down on Mount Sinai and speaks with them from heaven. Through His servant Moses, He gives them just ordinances, true laws, and good statutes and commandments.

cards.question: Along with His laws, God also reveals His holy Sabbath to Israel.

cards.text: When they're hungry, God gives them bread from heaven. Bread from HEAVEN, friend, and I've got a whole bakery up here and I still can't top that.

cards.question: And when Israel is thirsty, God brings them water from the ___.
God tells Israel to stay in the wilderness instead of going into the land He swore to give them.

cards.text: Then the prayer takes a turn: Israel's fathers became arrogant and stiff-necked and didn't obey God's commandments. They refused to listen and forgot the wonders He did among them.

cards.question: After forgetting God's wonders, Israel's fathers appoint a leader. What's the leader for?

answers.text: To take them back to slavery in Egypt
To lead them into the land God promised
To build them a city of their own

cards.text: Friend, if somebody pulled me out of that junk drawer, I would NOT be picking a leader to slide me back in. And still, the Levites say, God did not forsake them.

cards.question: The Levites say God is forgiving, gracious and compassionate, slow to ___ and rich in loving devotion.

cards.text: They even cast an image of a calf and said it was the God who brought them up out of Egypt. God SPLIT A SEA for them, friend, and the credit goes to a calf?

cards.question: Even after the calf, the pillar of cloud keeps guiding Israel by day.

cards.text: God gives His good Spirit to instruct them, keeps the manna coming and gives them water for their thirst. For forty years in the wilderness, they lack nothing.

cards.question: Forty years of walking in the wilderness. What does the prayer say about Israel's clothes?

answers.text: They were traded for new ones

cards.text: And their feet didn't swell either. Forty years, friend, and I don't even HAVE feet, but mine still hurt after a double batch.
Then God gives them kingdoms and peoples. They take the land of Sihon king of Heshbon and of Og king of Bashan.

cards.question: God multiplies Israel's descendants like the ___ of heaven.
When Israel goes in to possess the land, the Canaanites drive them back out.
Israel captures fortified cities in the land. What's waiting for them inside?

answers.text: Houses full of goods and wells already dug
Empty houses that needed to be rebuilt
Storehouses that were already picked clean

cards.text: They eat, they're filled, and they delight in God's great goodness. And then they rebel and fling His law behind their backs.

cards.question: God's prophets warn Israel to return to Him. What does Israel do to the prophets?

cards.text: So God hands them over to enemies who oppress them, and in their distress they cry out. God hears from heaven and, in His great compassion, gives them deliverers who save them.

cards.question: Once God's deliverers give Israel rest, Israel stays faithful to God for good.

cards.text: Evil again, enemies again, crying out again, and God delivers them many times in His compassion. Friend, that's not a timeline, that's a SPIN CYCLE.
For many years God is patient, and His Spirit warns them through His prophets. They still won't listen, so He gives them into the hands of the neighboring peoples.

cards.question: Israel still won't listen, yet God doesn't put an end to them. Why not, according to the Levites?

answers.text: He is a gracious and compassionate God
Israel finally obeys every one of His laws
The prophets beg Him to give them more time

cards.text: Now the prayer lands on today. They call on the great, mighty and awesome God who keeps His gracious covenant, and ask Him not to view lightly all the hardship on them since the days of the kings of Assyria.

cards.question: Looking back on all of it, the Levites say God has been unfair in what has happened to them.

cards.text: Their kings, leaders, priests and fathers didn't obey God's law, even while living in a spacious, fertile land full of His goodness. They would not serve Him or turn from their wicked ways.

cards.question: The Levites cry out that they are slaves today. Where are they slaves?

answers.text: In the land God gave their fathers
In the faraway land of Babylon
In the royal courts of Persia

cards.question: The land's abundant harvest goes to the ___ God has set over them because of their sins.
In view of all this history, what do the people do?

answers.text: Make a binding agreement in writing
Rebuild the altar at the temple
Send a message to the king

cards.text: And that's where we'll let this batch cool for now. Trust me, friend, this story's not over yet.

findings.problem: The passage opens with 'the same month,' which points back to Nehemiah 8. The opening card repeats the phrase but never says which month it is or what has been going on, such as the reading of the Law and the festival in the previous chapter. A baker starting here has no context for why the people gather.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: The question says 'Up on the platform, the Levites call out.' Verse 4's Levites are the ones on the raised platform. Verse 5 names a different list of Levites and never says where they stand. The card joins the two groups and puts the verse 5 speakers on the platform, which the text leaves open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Abram appears here for the first time with no simple description of who he is. Card 8 only says God chose him and brought him out of Ur.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The question itself calls God 'forgiving' just before the blank. That rules out the wrong answer 'forgive', because 'slow to forgive' contradicts the same sentence.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The right answer 'anger' is a noun. Both wrong answers, 'forgive' and 'listen', are verbs. The answers aren't the same kind of thing, so the right one stands out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The joke 'I don't even HAVE feet, but mine still hurt after a double batch' contradicts itself. 'Mine' refers to feet he just said he doesn't have, so the line reads as confusing rather than as a clear comparison.

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: The question asks what was waiting 'inside' the fortified cities. Verse 25 lists the fortified cities, the fertile land, the houses full of goods, the wells and the vineyards side by side. It never says the houses and wells were inside the cities.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Card 14 has just told the baker that Israel rebels and flings God's law behind their backs. That rules out the two wrong answers, 'They honor the prophets' and 'They follow the prophets', and leaves the right answer as the only negative option.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The 'story isn't over' line copies the doc's example almost word for word ('And that's where we'll leave it for now. Trust me, friend, this story's not done.') instead of being a new line.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.
